Q: CRC32 MPEG-2 Algorithm Implementation on FPGA A:

You currently take a 32-bit input (32 IBUFs), and produce a 32-bit output (32 OBUFs). You store a current 32-bit word (32 flops). You generate 32 operations between the bits of the polynomial and the bits of the data (32 LUTs).

Glancing at your resource list, it looks like that already accounts for something like 2/3rds to 3/4ths of your resource usage. To get much reduction in resource usage, you're doing to have to change at least one of those basic characteristics.

But you pretty much to store the current word, and have some representation of the bits of the polynomial, and something to XOR the necessary bits. That leaves the input and output as the main areas where you can save much.

Q: Why does this assignment fail but not cause an error? A:

This:

var[1] = 2

Is a special assignment syntax that is translated to a call to __setitem__:

var.__setitem__(1, 2)

You can't simply say that in one case [x][0] evaluated to 0 so [x][0] = 1 is equivalent to 0 = 1. The compiler looks at the full context and decides that that's an assignment of an item.

Q: In JavaScript is it bad practice to use ` ` every single time instead of "" or ''? A:

I seriously doubt this is really true; a string quoted with backticks will be parsed character-by-character like any other string, and when the parser instantiates the actual string value it will know whether it's really a template or not. I would be extremely surprised if the major JavaScript engines didn't handle the case properly. (Note that I don't think it's a great idea to always use backquotes, mostly because of the typing awkwardness.)

Q: Query to get inactive accounts in oracle table A:

This is one more example for these "advice" / "best practice" requests being a bad idea.

With an ordinary request instead, you'd get answers that other users rank and comment and you'd pick the best answer marking it as most appropriate for future readers.

Here in contrast, we don't even know whether the issue is settled.

So: if you still need help with this, write a regular request.
